source: Holton, Mackridge & Philippaki-Warburton, Greek: An Essential Grammar, 2nd ed. (Routledge, 2016), upload 3b712c2e ('last third, part 1'); PDF pp. 32-45 = Ch. 9 (§9.1-9.3.7). Copyrighted, no open license: rules restated in our own words; examples kept to short phrases/sentences.

sections.title: Co-ordinating conjunctions
sections.rule: Co-ordinating conjunctions join two phrases or two independent clauses. Use in clauses: §10.21.

list.en: and (optionally κι before a vowel in colloquial usage)

kai_as_too.rule: και before a noun phrase, strong pronoun, adjective, adverb or prepositional phrase means 'too, also'. Before numerals with the article it can mean 'both' or 'all'; after a numeral, with heavy stress, 'at least'.

examples.en: Mary came too.
It's big too.
We had rain here too.
We had rain in Athens too.
both of the children
all three of us
(S)he's at least thirty.

idioms.el: – Γύρισε ο μπαμπάς μου. – Ε και;
idioms.en: 'My dad's come back.' 'What of it?' (ε και; = so what?)

sections.concessive_uses: κι αν, κι ας, αν και, και να introduce concessive clauses (§10.14).

sections.title: Subordinating conjunctions
sections.rule: Overview of the main subordinators by function (uses in §10.9-10.19).

groups.items: όποιος 'whoever', ό,τι 'what(ever)', όσος 'however much; as much... as' (§10.9)
όπου 'where(ever)', όποτε 'whenever', όπως 'however', όσο 'however much; as much as' (§10.9)
πού 'where', πότε 'when', πώς 'how', πόσο 'how much', γιατί 'why' (§10.10.2)
αν, εάν, άμα 'if'; εφόσον 'provided that'; είτε... είτε 'whether... or...'; εκτός (κι) αν 'unless' (§10.13)
ακόμη κι αν, κι ας 'even if/though'; αν και 'although'; παρ' όλο που, μ' όλο που 'even though' (§10.14)
όταν 'when'; όποτε 'whenever'; μόλις 'as soon as'; πριν 'before'; αφού, μετά που 'after'; ώσπου, μέχρι που/να 'until'; ενώ, την ώρα που 'while'; καθώς 'as'; όσο 'as long as' (§10.15)
γιατί, διότι 'because'; επειδή, αφού, μια και/που 'since' (§10.19)
σαν να 'as if, as though'; παρά (να) '(rather) than' (§10.22)

sections.title: Particles (overview)
sections.rule: Greek particles are versatile little words that rarely match English words exactly. Seven groups: the future particle θα; the subjunctive particles να and ας; the negative particles δεν, μην and μη; the complementizer/relative particle που; the response particles ναι and όχι; the deictic particle να; the hortatory particle για.

sections.title: The future particle θα
sections.rule: θα stands before any finite verb form and can be separated from it only by weak pronouns. It mainly marks future time; perfective future = θα + dependent, imperfective future = θα + present; conditional = θα + imperfect; perfect conditional = θα + pluperfect (§6.5). It also expresses probability, most typically with the simple past, perfect and pluperfect, equivalent to English 'must (have)'; the tense is the same as for a definite statement.

examples.el: Θα του έδωσε εκείνος τα λεφτά.
examples.en: He must have given him the money himself.

examples.el: Θα έχει βρέξει, γιατί τα φύλλα είναι βρεμένα.
examples.en: It must have rained, because the leaves are wet.

examples.el: Θα είχε βρέξει, γιατί τα φύλλα ήταν βρεμένα.
examples.en: It must have rained, because the leaves were wet.

sections.title: The subjunctive particles να and ας
sections.rule: The subjunctive is any finite verb form (not imperative) preceded by να or ας. Such verbs are negated by μην (not δεν) and nothing but μην or weak pronouns may separate the particle from the verb.

uses.use: να in main clauses: suggestions, wishes, requests, certain commands and prohibitions (§10.3-10.4)

examples.en: Let me give them to you (offer or promise).
Should I give them to you?
You should give them to me.
(S)he shouldn't give them to him.
Oh, if only I could see you!

uses.use: να after question words, in questions not expecting an answer (often 'what are we to do', 'how am I supposed to know')

examples.en: What are we to do?
Where can (s)he/it have gone, I wonder?
How am I supposed to know?

uses.use: να-clauses as subject or complement: after verbs of wanting, hoping, promising, suggesting, trying; after μπορώ and πρέπει; after verbs of perception; after αρχίζω, σταματώ/παύω, συνεχίζω/εξακολουθώ (verb in the να-clause is almost always dependent or present; always present after beginning/stopping/continuing verbs)

examples.en: I wanted to speak to him urgently.
I hope to come tomorrow.

examples.el: Υποσχέθηκε να μη μου χαλάσει τα σχέδια.
examples.en: (S)he promised not to spoil my plans.

examples.el: Πρότεινε να πάμε μαζί στο πάρτι.
examples.en: (S)he suggested that we (should) go to the party together.

examples.el: Προσπαθούσε να βρει λύσεις για όλα τα προβλήματά του.
examples.en: (S)he was trying to find solutions to all his problems.
I was able to do what(ever) I wanted.
We must leave immediately.
We had to leave immediately.
We should leave immediately.

examples.el: Τον άκουσα να λέει πολλά δυσάρεστα πράγματα.
examples.en: I heard him say many unpleasant things.
They started running.
It stopped raining.
(S)he went on reading.

uses.note: μπορώ takes να in any person, number and tense except the perfect tenses; πρέπει exists only in present, imperfect, future and conditional.

uses.use: να in indirect questions; as complement of nouns and adjectives; after certain prepositions (αντί, για, δίχως, μέχρι, σαν, χωρίς)

examples.en: We didn't know what to do.

examples.el: Είναι καθαρή ανοησία να υποφέρεις έτσι.
examples.en: It's pure stupidity (for you) to suffer like this.

examples.el: Είναι δυνατόν να μη με θυμούνται;
examples.en: Is it possible (that) they don't remember me?

uses.use: πρέπει να expressing probability (like θα): verb in the να-clause usually simple past, perfect or pluperfect; negation in either clause

examples.el: Πρέπει να έχουν γυρίσει από τις διακοπές.
examples.en: They must have come back from holiday.

examples.el: Δεν πρέπει να έχουν γυρίσει ακόμα από τις διακοπές.
examples.en: They mustn't/can't have come back from holiday yet.

examples.el: Πρέπει να γυρίζουν τώρα από τις διακοπές.
examples.en: They must be on their way back from holiday now.

uses.use: μπορεί να expressing possibility (3rd sg. present), can stand alone as 'maybe'. Negating the να-verb gives 'may not'; negating μπορεί gives 'can't'

examples.el: Μπορεί να έχουν γυρίσει από τις διακοπές.
examples.en: Maybe they've come back from holiday.

examples.el: Μπορεί να μην έχουν γυρίσει από τις διακοπές.
examples.en: They may not have come back from holiday.

examples.el: Δεν μπορεί να έχουν γυρίσει από τις διακοπές.
examples.en: They can't have come back from holiday.

uses.use: ας: main clauses only; commands, permission, suggestions, wishes. Less pressing than να (command mixed with permission or indifference). Frequent after και/κι in concessives; ας + imperfect = wish about the past

examples.en: Let's leave this subject.

examples.el: Ας φωνάζει ο Πέτρος όσο θέλει.
examples.en: Let Peter shout as much as he likes.
Let them come if they want.

examples.el: Ας μη μου τα δώσει, αφού δεν θέλει.
examples.en: Let him/her not give them to me, since (s)he doesn't want to.

examples.el: Μάλλον θα γίνει πόλεμος, κι ας μην το θέλουμε.
examples.en: War will probably happen, even if we don't want it (to).
If only you hadn't listened to him.

sections.title: The negative particles δεν, μην and μη
sections.rule: Indicative verbs are negated by δεν; subjunctive verbs (after να or ας) by μην. μην may drop final -ν before certain letters (§1.6). μην also introduces negative commands (§10.4) and cannot be separated from the verb except by weak pronouns. When negating items other than verbs, μη has no final -ν (§10.7.7); it can stand alone as 'Don't!'.

examples.en: (S)he won't come.
(S)he shouldn't come.

sections.title: The complementizer and relative particle που
sections.rule: που has three chief functions: introducing a complement clause (§10.12), a result clause (§10.18), or a relative clause (§4.7, §10.9).

examples.el: Λυπάμαι που δεν μπόρεσα να έρθω στο πάρτι.
examples.en: I'm sorry (that) I wasn't able to come to your party.

examples.el: Φώναξα τόσο πολύ που δεν μπορώ να μιλήσω.
examples.en: I shouted so much (that) I can't speak.

examples.el: Ο άντρας που ήρθε είναι ο πεθερός μου.
examples.en: The man who came is my father-in-law.

sections.title: The response particles ναι and όχι
sections.rule: ναι 'yes' and όχι 'no' answer questions; όχι can also negate any part of speech (§7.2) or a whole clause (§10.5.1).

sections.title: The deictic particle να
sections.rule: Spelled like the subjunctive particle, deictic να means 'there (is)' when pointing something out; alone, or followed by a noun phrase or a nominative weak pronoun (§4.1).

examples.en: That's the problem!
There he is!

sections.title: The hortatory particle για
sections.rule: Colloquial για (spelled like the preposition) adds encouragement before an imperative.

examples.en: Do sit down!
